requirement: Immediate/deferred delivery and callback hits remain correct

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: fresh process: godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd (direct emit, then deferred emit, then one awaited process_frame)

obligations.note: _on_direct() body -- fires synchronously, inside the emit() call on line 17, before line 18 runs; the interleaving is only provable via expected_log_sequence, not this obligation alone
_on_deferred() body -- reached by process end, since the frame does turn in this run; whether it fired before or after the post-emit line is, again, only provable via the log, not this obligation

inputs.name: deferred_never_flushed
inputs.call: fresh process: godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd -- no_flush (quits immediately after the deferred emit, before any frame turns)

obligations.note: genuinely never reached in this run's own process: the frame never turns before quit(), so the deferred callback never fires. This is the real discriminating obligation -- a tool that treats CONNECT_DEFERRED delivery as synchronous would show this as a false_hit.

run_deferred() itself runs to completion, including line 24 -- emit() returns synchronously even for a deferred connection, it's only the CALLBACK delivery (line 12) that's queued, not the emit() call itself

notes: Both inputs are their own fresh process (per the F041 precedent): a single cumulative coverage report can only show whichever facts are true by process end, so 'the deferred callback never fired' can only be expressed by a process that quits before the frame that would have flushed it, not by an intermediate snapshot inside a longer-running process. default's obligations are all true and carry no discriminating power at the coverage level by themselves -- expected_log_sequence (fixture-specific, checked by the driver, not pilot/harness/comparator.py, same category as F013/F042's expected_log) is what actually proves the synchronous-vs-queued distinction for that run. deferred_never_flushed is what gives this fixture real coverage-level discriminating power, the same role F041's zero_instances input plays: a tool that (incorrectly) delivers CONNECT_DEFERRED callbacks synchronously would show a false_hit on line 12 in this run. Confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine via this fixture's own driver.gd.

ambiguities: Only connect()-time CONNECT_DEFERRED is tested, not the alternative call_deferred("emit_signal", ...) form (deferring the emit call itself rather than the delivery). Both are expected to behave the same way (queued until the next frame) but only one form is verified here.
